Use plots as diagnostics, then follow up

  • QC shifts: verify metric units, group sizes, and metadata; a batch shift can arise from technical or design differences, but a plot alone cannot identify its cause.
  • PCA separation: inspect the explained variance, sample labels, design balance, and component loadings. Consider the experimental model before choosing batch correction; indiscriminate correction can remove biological signal.
  • Fragmented UMAP: check feature selection, sample count, scaling, and parameter sensitivity. Raising n_neighbors broadens neighborhoods, while changing min_dist changes packing; neither guarantees meaningful clusters.
  • Uniform heatmap: check transformation, selected features, and color limits. Row scaling may reveal relative patterns while hiding absolute amplitude.
  • Volcano extremes: check missing or zero adjusted p-values, effect-size estimates, model formula, contrast, and multiplicity correction before labeling candidates.

Save the plotting code and intermediate coordinates alongside the figure. Captions should identify the dataset and number of samples, transformation and filtering, encoding and thresholds, package versions, and the main limitation. Use accessible palettes and do not encode an essential distinction by color alone.

What this run produced

These are the actual PNG files saved by the downloadable R Markdown lab, not illustrations. They use the supplied invented teaching tables. No biological observations or fitted differential-expression results are shown.

Run details and limits

The complete supplied R report rendered successfully with R 4.3.3, ggplot2 3.4.4, uwot 0.1.16, rmarkdown 2.25, and Pandoc 3.1.3 on Linux. All five Python plotting alternatives also ran on the same tables.

Checks confirmed six matching sample IDs, finite PCA and UMAP coordinates, and six non-empty figure files for each language. The volcano step omitted the one missing adjusted p-value. R and Python UMAP coordinates are not expected to match.

This verifies the supplied plotting exercise in this environment, not every possible input, operating system, or upstream biological analysis. Inspect the execution evidence.

References

  • R stats::prcomp documentation and the uwot package guide

Calculate LISI in R

The lisi package's compute_lisi() takes a matrix with cells in rows and embedding dimensions in columns, plus metadata with one row per cell. It returns one score column for each requested metadata label. The code below uses existing Seurat reductions and reorders metadata to match embedding row names before calculation. Replace the example metadata keys with columns present in your object.

# Outputs: lisi_scores.csv and lisi_metadata.csv; the input RDS is read only

Summarize by cluster without losing cell alignment

Run this summary as a separate Rscript process after the LISI calculation block completes. The first block saves the matched metadata to lisi_metadata.csv; this block reloads it instead of relying on an in-memory object from another process. Keep both CSV files in the working directory. The cell-name check stops on mismatched inputs rather than silently assigning scores by row position.

# Inputs: lisi_scores.csv and lisi_metadata.csv, written by the first block
meta <- read.csv("lisi_metadata.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
lisi_df <- read.csv("lisi_scores.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
if (!setequal(rownames(meta), rownames(lisi_df))) {
  stop("LISI output cells do not match the metadata cells")
}

8. Quick VAF distribution plot (example in R)

# Input: vcf/NA12878_pass.withVAF.tsv
# Output: diagnostics/VAF_distribution.png
Rscript -e '
d <- read.delim("vcf/NA12878_pass.withVAF.tsv", header = TRUE)
png("diagnostics/VAF_distribution.png", width = 800, height = 600)
hist(as.numeric(d$VAF[!is.na(d$VAF)]), breaks = 100, col = "steelblue",
     main = "VAF distribution", xlab = "VAF")
dev.off()
'

For a diploid, high-quality biallelic germline call, heterozygous and homozygous-alternate genotypes often have allele fractions near 0.5 and 1, respectively. A histogram is descriptive, not a genotype caller: depth, allele balance, ploidy, mapping/base quality, contamination, and capture bias affect the values. The included plot command assumes the table has a numeric VAF column and an existing diagnostics directory.

Output inspection and interpretation
